analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 2863-3240 and 3241-3640). The patch excerpt shows documentation-only edits, mainly cluster served-speed record scoping at head lines 4592-4608 and a tp-check --layer-stride note at about 4805. Those head lines fall outside the two supplied text units, so I could not inspect them directly; the patch excerpt is truncated. The supplied excerpts describe no new code paths, endpoints, key handling, or authorization changes.

Security-relevant statements I checked for consistency with the threat model:
- Native MiMo, Qwen4, coordinator-serving channels, and cluster member registration all retain fail-closed memory admission and ownership-until-retirement semantics.
- The cluster worker is launched by the installed owner with a fixed environment. Peer-supplied environment and launch arguments are explicitly rejected (about lines 3507-3519).
- Cluster prefix caching is keyed to the request's own partition, cache switch and tenant, carried from the leader (about lines 3289-3291). This is consistent with the T-041 coordinator-authored cacheSalt posture.
- Clone and dropCachedPages use msync(MS_INVALIDATE) without privileges and without following links (about lines 3372-3383).
- The MiMo video asset uses an in-memory URL and writes no payload to disk (about lines 3131-3136). This is consistent with T-050.
- Client-supplied reserved schema metadata is rejected, and tool schema restoration grants no bypass (about lines 3060-3063).
- The plan registration refuses unequal tensor-parallel shares for coordinator-scoped clusters, because the provider does not encode the shares (about lines 3230-3240).

I saw no regression, invalidated assumption or new attack surface in the supplied text. Remaining unverified items, which are outside the supplied evidence:
- The code behind the described behaviors (ClusterServedSpeedRecords, ClusterPlacementFlow, NativePairMemberRoster, etc.) is not shown.
- The unseen patch hunks at head lines 4592-4891, 6725-6735, 6858-6894, 7318-7323 and 7444-7454 were not available to me.
- There is no evidence that the documentation overclaims a security property.
